title: Workload-Adaptive Scheduling for Efficient Use of Parallel File Systems in High-Performance Computing Clusters
problem: Contention in shared bandwidth-type storage systems like Lustre significantly impacts HPC job runtimes. Users lack accurate methods to estimate job I/O requirements, complicating scheduling decisions.
motivation: Optimizing parallel file system usage through intelligent scheduling is critical for improving performance and resource efficiency in HPC clusters.
method: The system watches how much data is moving through Lustre (a shared file system used in computing clusters) right now and estimates how much storage each job needs. It then tells Slurm (the job scheduler) to reschedule jobs to prevent the storage from being over- or under-used. A two-group technique handles edge cases where some jobs don't use any storage.
key_novelty: The system automatically adjusts job scheduling based on actual real-time storage usage, eliminating the need for users to predict how much storage their jobs will need.
contributions: I/O-aware scheduling framework integrated into Slurm
Real-time Lustre bandwidth monitoring and dynamic job I/O requirement estimation
Two-group approximation technique for handling zero-throughput jobs
Prototype validation on real HPC clusters
